What is the maximum number of unique harbor locations that the red player can have a settlement/city on by the end of the turn, given the player rolls a 6 in this turn? Also make sure that there is at least one resource card of each type by the end of this turn.  Return the answer in the following format: [prev_harbors: <number of harbors with the players city/settlements before the turn>, new_harbors: <number of harbors with the players city/settlements after the turn>]
Rationale: According to the given board stateIn the question, The red player has three settlements. The red player currently hasThe following resource cards: [bricks: 3, wool: 4, grains: 4, lumber: 3, ore: 3]. Since the player rolls is 6, the player would get 1 brick resource card. This would result in the player having [brick: 4, wool: 4, grain: 4, lumber: 3, ore: 3]. Use the development card: year of plenty, to get 1 lumber and 1 brick resource cards. Build 1 (by paying 1 brick, lumber, wool, and grain) settlement in the (8,10) special harbor location. Use 1 brick and 1 lumber to build a road (along the coast of forest containing 8), then build another settlement on the special harbor (8, 4). This way the red player can get access to 2 more unique harbors. This way the maximum number of unique harbors the player would get access to by the end of this turn is 3.
